text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Incident created — High 5xx rate on api.redwood.io
IncidentBot: Priority: P1. Pager: @Amanda oncall. Detection: spike in 5xx from chat endpoints, elevated queue depth.
Amanda: I'm on it, checking dashboards now.
Raj: I can grab traffic shaping and routing. Heads-up: embeddings also showing latency tail but lower error rate.
Amanda: Confirming errors are concentrated on /v1/chat and /v1/chat/stream. Rerank appears unaffected so far.
Jess: Copy. Any customer reports? Support triage says a handful of API keys reporting timeouts, some cancelled streaming sessions.
ops-bot: Deployed alerting rule triggered: chat-5xx-rate > 5% for > 2m. Trace IDs sample: 0c1a2b3c..0f9e.
Tom: Logs show upstreams returning 503s from nodepool-gpu-3. Possible OOM on a variant running quantized kernels.
Amanda: Rolling a quick healthcheck script to list node memory pressure. Running: ```kubectl get pods -l app=inference -o wide``` 
Amanda: Got nodes with high oom_kill counts on gpularge-2 zone.
Raj: Working mitigation plan: 1) Per-endpoint emergency quotas — throttle chat for non-enterprise to 30rps per API key; 2) Disable rerank-forced fallback that spawns heavy model; 3) Route traffic for enterprise keys to dedicated pool.
Jess: Agree. We should preserve embeddings for billing-critical workflows, but lower concurrency there too. Suggest embeddings to 10rps per-key for now.
Amanda: Oncall handoff note: I'm paging infra to look at node health. Raj, can you apply rate limits via gateway so we don't redeploy? Use `redwoodctl gateway rate-limit`.
Raj: Applying gateway rules now. Command: ```redwoodctl gateway rate-limit set --route "/v1/chat" --scope non-enterprise --rps 30 --burst 60 --reason "P1 - emergency chat throttle"``` 
Raj: Rule applied. Confirming in UI: chat non-enterprise -> 30 rps.
Tom: Saw immediate drop in error rate on one cluster. Queue depth falling.
Amanda: Now disable heavy rerank fallback for public tier: ```redwoodctl config set --path features.rerank.fallback --value false --env prod``` 
Raj: Disabled. Pushed config, canarying to 5% traffic in region-us-west.
ops-bot: Canary rollout started: rerank.fallback=false -> 5% traffic.
Jess: Support update drafted: "We are applying temporary rate limits to chat and embeddings for non-enterprise customers to stabilize service. Enterprise traffic routed to dedicated capacity. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes." Approving to send.
Amanda: Approve. Post the message to #support and #status once we confirm metrics.
Raj: Next step: apply embeddings limit: ```redwoodctl gateway rate-limit set --route "/v1/embeddings" --scope public --rps 10 --burst 30 --reason "P1 - embeddings throttle"``` 
Raj: Embeddings rule live.
Tom: Metrics: chat 5xx down from 9% -> 1.8% over last 2m. Embeddings latency tail reduced slightly.
Lee: Note: some customers might hit quota errors. Can we add a short grace window header telling clients to retry after X seconds? Gateway supports `Retry-After` injection.
Raj: Adding `Retry-After` header 5s for throttled responses: ```redwoodctl gateway header set --route "/v1/chat" --on-throttle "Retry-After: 5"``` 
Raj: Header set.
Amanda: Running customer impact sweep: list of top 20 API keys by error volume. Key abcd1234 (Acme) spiked 500 errors; they've got enterprise flag. Routing check shows they were hitting public pool due to stale routing rule.
Jess: I'll open a ticket to support Acme and offer to move them to dedicated pool; pragmatic fix: temporary quota bump for that key.
Raj: Temporarily granting quota bump to abcd1234 to avoid impacting their SLAs: ```redwoodctl quota set --key abcd1234 --route "/v1/chat" --limit 200rps --duration 2h --reason "P1 - emergency"``` 
ops-bot: Quota change recorded by ops (change-id: chg-20260323-95c).
Tom: After quota bump and routing correction, Acme errors stopped.
Amanda: Good. Next, monitor for noisy tenants — if a single key is responsible for >30% of chat traffic we should throttle it specifically.
Jess: Support outbound: posted statement to customers affected, included troubleshooting steps and ETA 30m.
Amanda: On-call handover: I'll be handing to Raj in 25 minutes; current state: traffic mitigations in place, errors trending down, canary OK. Logging notes in incident board.
Raj: I'll take primary after the handoff. Action items for next 30m: continue canary from 5%->50% if stable, evaluate whether to keep rerank disabled, and prepare rollback plan.
Amanda: Adding checkpoint — if 5xx <1% for 30m, we can relax chat throttle to 60rps and embeddings to 20rps for public.
Tom: Infra is redeploying a patched runtime variant to gpularge-2 with memory fix. ETA 18m.
ops-bot: Patch deployment started: rollout group gpu-fix -> 3 nodes. Watch pods for CrashLoopBackOff.
Raj: Noted. Preparing docs for permanent route-specific limits: we'll propose default public quotas: chat 50rps, embeddings 20rps, rerank disabled by default for free tier. That's for post-mortem.
Amanda: Checlist: record timestamps, changes applied, config diffs. Make sure incident timeline saved to #postmortems.
Jess: I'll draft the initial postmortem after incident stabilizes; include customer impact assessment and mitigation chronology.
Tom: Observability note — add fine-grained SLOs per-route next quarter so we can alert before whole-pool collapse.
Amanda: Handoff to Raj now. Raj, you're primary, call me if anything spikes.
Raj: Taking over. Continuing monitoring. Current metrics snapshot: chat 5xx=0.9%, embeddings errors=0.4%, rerank errors=0.1%. Canary at 5% stable.
Amanda: Thanks team. Leaving detailed notes in thread. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Stabilizing. Severity remains P1 until 2h stable.
Jess: Sending updated customer note now."
